notes.reason: The sentence is a quotation from the Offrange article "This Land is Their Land", but Andy does adopt the number for his own argument: "The 8 million-gallon data center is 0.4% of that. This data center is using as much water as a local 35 acre irrigated farm." So the number is fair game in principle. The note fails on correctness and fairness. "Upwards of 8 million gallons" is a floor, and the floor is well sourced: the article links it to a WPR story (17 Sep 2025) reporting that Microsoft's closed-loop Mount Pleasant data centers will need up to 8.4 million gallons a year, so a hyperscale campus really can run at that level. The note's "typically far more" rests on Google, whose evaporatively cooled sites average 550,000 gallons a day (its 2.8 million a day for Council Bluffs matches Google's 2025 report), but that is the most water-hungry operator, and the facility Andy is actually writing about is the Wolcott campus in White County, whose project site promises closed-loop cooling with "zero water for cooling". Andy has written at length on data center water and would answer that the note swaps in the wrong kind of facility; the fairer correction, that the 35-acre-farm comparison only holds for closed-loop designs while evaporative sites use tens to hundreds of millions of gallons a year, is not the note that was written.
